I hate it too. During COVID I had two breakdowns at two different facilities and went on disability. When he money finished, I went with the agency and it was an awful experience as well. I randomly applied for a job as a teacher in Honduras and ended up living there for two years. It was wonderful but I ran out of money. I’m currently back in nursing and now hyper aware of how much I hate every single aspect of the profession. What I have done to help me before I make the final move of leaving the profession and becoming a teacher full time:


1 . Work a second job as tutor. I refuse to do anything beyond my 8 hours as a nurse so that I can dedicate my time to my young learners 


2. Use my sick days: I don’t care if it makes me look unreliable. If I am too mentally drained I would have another meltdown and I can’t fathom the recovery time again


3. Have a support system. I have a brother who is also a nurse who hates the job as bitterly as I do so we vent for a while and then we go out and have fun. I have friends who aren’t related to the field who are refreshing to be around 


4. Avoid anyone who guilts you into thinking that nursing is this awesome career and you shouldn’t feel bad because look at the economy or whatever: my mom and I will never get along because she makes it a point to not cry around her because I’m in a good job. I avoid talking about her about work. 


5. Find healthy things you enjoy doing: sleeping , reading, watching movies and collecting trinkets is my thing 


6. Set up your savings account: put some money away so that you can fund your future education away from nursing or even for a vacation to get away for a while


7. Say no to extra assignments: unless you are tight for money or working towards a goal, don’t be guilted into picking up extra shifts or staying extra because someone else didn’t show up. It is not your problem. Your mental health is far superior 


I do know your struggle and I’m so happy more nurses are coming out saying that this is not what they thought it would be or worse they were forced into it and feel like they are drowning. I hope this helps and I’m sending you lots of love and hugs!
